Exercise 1: C-S-T-A for your own org

html:
Theory is proven in production-shaped scenarios. This phase presents the four flagship use cases that tie the whole roadmap together — UC1 Retail, UC2 Financial Services, UC3 Telco/Health, and UC4 Manufacturing — each as a consultant brief you will solve in Phase 18. The exam's "Solution Positioning" domain is literally this skill: map a business problem to the correct Data 360 configuration.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Read a business brief and extract a precise, exam-style requirement statement.
  • Name the data sources, DMOs/DLOs, identity/transforms, segments, activations, and data actions a solution needs.
  • Spot the constraint traps (consent, data space, real-time vs batch, retention, brand rules) that decide an answer.
  • Carry one case from brief → architecture, then grade your work against Phase 18's solution key.

1. How to read a use-case brief (the consulting reflex)

Every brief hides 5 W's + 1 constraint. Use the C-S-T-A checklist before proposing anything:

LetterQuestionExample
CCustomer/identity — who is resolved?IndividualId, Contact against web visitors
SSource — what were the data in what system?Order soql, web events, CRM cases, marketing sends
TTransform — what change happens to the data?Unify, standardize, calculate (LTV, churn)
AAct — what is the business outcome?Send a journey, update a Case, notify, report
+Constraintconsent / data space / retention / real-time / budget"cannot see marketing", "must react in minutes", "GDPR"

Then voice the architecture in one sentence: "We ingest {S} with {connector}, unify under identity resolution via {key}, compute {T} as a calculated insight, build the {segment}, publish via {activation} to {target}, and trigger {data action} when the segment qualifies — subject to {consent/data-space}." If you can say it in one breath, you understand the case.

2. UC1 — Retail omnichannel win-back

Brief: A fashion retailer has order data in its ERP (CSV exports nightly), web browsing events via the Ingestion API (streaming), and marketing sends in Marketing Cloud. They want a "win-back" journey to Gold-tier customers who bought 5+ times but haven't ordered in 60 days, offering an incentive before they defect. Marketing must not see purchasing history; service may.

CSTA
IndividualId (email + loyalty ID resolution)ERP orders (CSV nightly), web events (streaming), MC sendsUnify profile; Recency = days since last order; OrderCount = 5+; Tier = GoldSegment "Win-Back Eligible" → MCE data extension → journey; consent Email apply

Constraint: marketing space must NOT see order history (only the activation attributes); real-time for the web-intent kicker, batch OK for the 60-day rule.

3. UC2 — Financial services: compliance + churn alert

Brief: A bank unites checking, cards, and loans from 3 legacy systems. They need a churn-risk score driving a prioritized servicing team, and a single-consent withdrawal respected across all channels (email + SMS + app push). Regulators require lineage and audit.

CSTA
IndividualId via official ID + tax ID matchCore (nightly), cards (real-time POS), loans (daily), omnichannel consentBalanceTrend, SpendVelocity, ChurnScore (Einstein model, Phase 13)Segment "At-Risk Gold" → Case update via data action → retriever-grounded agent (Phase 14)

Constraint: consent categories isolated per channel; retention per DLO (cards 90d, core 7y); audit artifacts (activation runs, consent captures) retained; agent must not see card limits.

4. UC3 — Telco/Healthcare: 360 profile for self-service

Brief: A telco (or patient-portal operator) wants a unified profile in a self-service console, so a customer can see usage, billed devices, and open tickets in one view — with an Agentforce assistant that answers "when will my device be replaced?" using documents (warranty PDFs, SLA docs) and live account data.

CSTA
IndividualId via subscriber IDBilling (daily), usage (streaming), tickets (CRM), warranty PDFs (file ingestion)Standardize usage; profile attributes (device, plan); Data Graph nodesConsole Data 360 components + Agentforce grounded on retriever over PDFs + Apex billing action

Constraint: data spaces — the assistant may read warranty/SLA docs and own-account data ONLY; consent for future promo activation separate from self-service display.

5. UC4 — Manufacturing: unified account for field service

Brief: A manufacturer links order management (ERP), IoT sensor telemetry (streaming), and field-service cases to a unified account. Priority plating: if a machine's telemetry crosses a maintenance threshold, open/escalate the case and page the field manager — near-real-time.

CSTA
AccountId (ERP + telemetry device serial → account) resolutionERP orders (hourly), telemetry (streaming IoT), cases (CRM)Real-time insight "Maintenance_Score > 80"Data action: Case priority=P1 + Slack/page update challenge (webhook) ; segment "Flash Maintenance" for dispatch

Constraint: the telemetry→account join is the hard problem (device serial vs account hierarchy); the real-time chain must be streaming end-to-end.

6. Choosing the constraints that trip candidates

The four classic trap constraints — if you see them you've found your exam answer:

  1. "Real-time" → every hop streaming (ingestion, transform/insight, dynamic segment, activation/action). Static segment or nightly batch kills it.
  2. "Cannot see X" / GDPR / consent → data space boundary + consent categories + suppression before activation; not a "fix the report" answer.
  3. "No write-back" / "live view" → on-the-fly Data 360 components, NOT materialization into CRM.
  4. "Retention" → per-object retention; predict data-availability consequences, don't length-one-size-all.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: C-S-T-A for your own org

Write the C/S/T/A table + one-sentence architecture for your company's highest-value use case. If you don't have one, use UC4.

Exercise 2: Constraint hunt

Under each UC above, bold the constraint that most likely changes the answer. For UC2 write why the agent can't see "card limits" (answer: data-space + field-level security) and what the assistant should be scoped to.

Exercise 3: Force-app mapping

For UC4, name the Apex/objects/actions in this repo that would implement each hop (e.g. telemetry ingestion → DataCloudIngestionService; score → CalculatedInsightService; case → DataActionHandlerService). Is a Maintenance_Score calculated insight the same as a segment? (Hint: insight ≠ segment — reference Phases 5 and 6.)

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Use case (UC)End-to-end business scenario solved with Data 360 + Salesforce automation.
BriefConsultant-facing requirement statement (context, data, outcome, constraints).
C-S-T-A checklistCustomer / Source / Transform / Act (+ constraint) reading structure.
Constraint trapThe hidden rule (real-time, consent, data space, retention) that decides the correct answer.
Unified AccountIdentity resolution at the account level (ERP + IoT + CRM).
Lineage & audit artifactsThe retained proof regulators (and the exam) want: activation runs, consent captures, data-action logs.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can extract the 5 W's + constraint from any brief.
  • I can write a one-sentence architecture for a use case.
  • I can name sources/DMOs/insights/segments/activations/actions per case.
  • I can spot all four trap constraints and avoid them.

Self-Check

  1. Q: What's the first step for ANY brief? — A: The C-S-T-A checklist — identify the identity, sources, transforms, and outcomes plus the constraint before proposing architecture.
  2. Q: UC1 — why can't sales see order history? — A: Data-space boundary (marketing space leaf-level attributes only + activation attribute list), not a layer fix.
  3. Q: The single-word kill shot for "real-time"? — A: Batch — real-time requires streaming ingestion, a streaming transform/insight, a dynamic segment, and a streaming-capable action end-to-end.
